actions.name: Occurs in at least one protected area

documentation.range: This species has a disjunct distribution, having been recorded from isolated localities in Tanzania, Kenya, Uganda and the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (Spawls and Branch 2020).  There is only a single record for each of both Kenya and Tanzania and only two localities are known from central Uganda, with the remaining Ugandan observations from the southwest portion of the country. It occurs between 900 and 2,500 m asl.
documentation.population: There is little information available on the abundance or population trends of this species. It is a rare species in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. In Kakamega Forest in Kenya, populations appear to go through yearly changes in abundance, for unknown reasons (Spawls and Branch 2020).
documentation.habitats: Overall little is known of its natural history. This species has been recorded from both primary and secondary forest, and in cultivated shrubland known as "agricultural forest" (P. Wagner pers. comm. 2014). It is found in tall grasses, papyrus, bushes, creepers and small trees (Spawls and Branch 2020), always in association with water bodies such as rivers, ponds and streams (P. Wagner pers. comm. 2014). It gives birth to live young.
documentation.threats: There are not believed to be any major threats to this species.
documentation.measures: This species occurs in Kakamega Forest Reserve, Kenya, Bwindi Impenetrable Forest National Park and Kigezi Game Park, Uganda and Minziro Forest Reserve, Tanzania. More studies into the distribution are needed, as is additional work on the natural history of this snake.
documentation.use_trade: This species is occasionally found in the pet trade. Numbers involved are low (Jensen et al. 2018 report 45 live animals advertised for sale between 2013 and 2017 across four African states), and so this is not thought to be affecting the population.
documentation.rationale: Listed as Least Concern in view of its wide distribution, presumed large overall population, and because it is unlikely to be declining fast enough to qualify for listing in a more threatened category.
